title: The article discusses the establishment of the United States Africa Command (Africom) announced by President Bush in 2007. Africom was created in response to various challenges in Africa, including poverty, corruption, and internal conflicts, which the U.S. government claims could lead to exploitation by extremist groups. However, there are concerns that Africom may represent a militarization of U.S. foreign policy in Africa and serve the interests of the military-industrial complex. The article highlights the historical context of U.S. military operations in Africa, noting that prior to Africom, military activities were managed by separate commands. Observers urge caution regarding the true intentions behind Africom.
